sections.heading: Choosing the Right Text for the Right Image
paragraphs: Effective captions consider contrast first: light text over dark areas and dark text over light areas guarantees legibility in any viewing condition.
For busy photographs, placing text on a subtle semi-transparent band or darkening the region behind the caption dramatically improves readability without obscuring the subject.
Font weight and character spacing matter as much as size; condensed bold faces suit banners while lighter weights fit elegant captions.
Testing two or three placements before committing is quick because every render is instant and local.

sections.heading: Watermarks and Brand Crediting
paragraphs: Photographers and creators protect their work with a discreet text watermark placed in a corner, typically the photographer's name or studio handle.
Because the text is baked into the exported pixels, it remains visible even when the image is shared elsewhere, deterring casual unauthorized reuse.
Semi-transparent watermarks balance visibility with aesthetics, marking ownership without ruining the view of the image itself.
Local processing ensures the original and branded export stay on your machine until you choose to share them.

sections.heading: Common Text Combinations That Work
paragraphs: A price or discount tag near a product photograph drives ecommerce listings. A holiday greeting over a celebratory photo personalizes seasonal posts.
Headline-plus-subtitle pairings suit blog cover images, where a short bold line is backed by a smaller supporting phrase.
For tutorial screenshots, numbered callouts typed directly onto the image reduce back-and-forth between the image and its caption text.
Repurposing the same base image with different text for several platforms is a fast way to localize or vary campaign creative.

sections.heading: Where Text on Images Matters Most
paragraphs: Ecommerce uploads nearly always pair a product photo with a short label: size, color or a special offer printed at the corner.
Event invitations gain clarity when the date, venue and time appear directly on the hero image rather than in a separate caption block.
Recipe steps, troubleshooting guides and safety instructions become scan-friendly when each instruction annotates its own photo.
Used consistently across a brand, styled text overlays also become a recognizable part of the visual identity.

sections.heading: Repurposing One Image Across Platforms
paragraphs: A single clean product shot can carry several messages: price for the store, a value promise for the ad and a size guide for the listing.
Starting from one master image and adding a distinct caption per platform keeps the brand look consistent while respecting each network's framing.
Geographic markets can receive localized wording without reshooting a single pixel.
The payback is a faster creative pipeline where the photograph stays fixed and only the message changes.
